name: SLPerf
description: Data privacy concerns has made centralized training of data, which is scattered across silos, infeasible, leading to the need for collaborative learning frameworks. To address that, two prominent frameworks emerged, i.e., federated learning (FL) and split learning (SL). While FL has established various benchmark frameworks and research libraries,SL currently lacks a unified library despite its diversity in terms of label sharing, model aggregation, and cut layer choice. This lack of standardization makes comparing SL paradigms difficult. To address this, we propose SLPerf, a unified research framework and open research library for SL, and conduct extensive experiments on four widely-used datasets under both IID and Non-IID data settings. Our contributions include a comprehensive survey of recently proposed SL paradigms, a detailed benchmark comparison of different SL paradigms in different situations, and rich engineering take-away messages and research insights for improving SL paradigms. SLPerf can facilitate SL algorithm development and fair performance comparisons. The code is available at https://github.com/Rainysponge/Split-learning-Attacks .
evaluation_method: accuracy for predictive tasks plus system-level metrics (communication cost, runtime, memory, and model convergence) reported separately
general_score_metric: accuracy (primary) with additional system metrics (communication cost, runtime) as co-primary metrics
reputation: A recent, research-focused unified library for split learning with limited but growing adoption in privacy-preserving ML research.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on split learning paradigms; reports both predictive and system-level metrics. Dataset sizes and experimental setups vary across splits, so cross-paper comparison requires care; reproducibility can depend on system configuration.
